channel.title: Sattaya.AI — Blog by Sattaya Singkul
channel.description: Writing on end-to-end AI products, voice assistants, LLM agents and on-premise AI in production.

item.title: TurboQuant, reviewed: when a theory paper walks straight into production
item.description: A close read of TurboQuant (ICLR 2026): random rotations, Lloyd–Max codebooks and a 1-bit QJL residual, and why it went from proof to vLLM and a 17k-star vector index within weeks.

item.title: Why emotion models fall apart outside the lab (and what actually helps)
item.description: Speech emotion recognition looks solved on benchmarks and breaks on real calls. A researcher's tour of domain shift, speaker leakage, metric learning and self-supervised features.

item.title: FinOps-Estimator: sizing GPUs for a voice AI pipeline
item.description: An open-source tool that turns concurrency and model choices for STT → LLM → TTS into VRAM, RAM, CPU, TFLOPS and cloud or on-prem cost.

item.title: Fitting an LLM in your own server room: the memory math behind on-prem AI
item.description: Bits per weight, quantization error, outliers, KV cache and memory bandwidth: how to decide which model actually runs on the GPUs you own.

item.title: Your MAU is not your load: capacity math for voice AI at scale
item.description: How to turn "a million users" into a latency budget, a concurrency number, KV-cache memory and a GPU count — with the formulas, not vibes.
